title: Guided KYC checklist + auto-resume reminder (D+2, D+5)
hypothesis: Many registrants stall at KYC because the document step is unclear; a pre-submission checklist with photo-quality checks and a resume reminder will raise KYC completion.
target_segment: New registrants, all channels (stratified by channel and device)
intervention: Show document checklist + capture-quality validation before upload; push/email/SMS resume reminder on day 2 and day 5 if KYC incomplete.
control_group: Current KYC screens and no reminder cadence beyond the existing default.
primary_metric: KYC completion within 14 days of registration
guardrail_metrics: KYC rejection / resubmission rate; KYC support tickets per 100 registrants; unsubscribe/opt-out rate
feasibility: Slow (14-26 weeks accrual): run concurrently with other tests or accept a larger MDE
expected_benefit: +5 pp in KYC completion is the ASSUMED target; at ~190 registrants/week this would add ~10 KYC-complete users/week.
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test (or chi-square) on 14-day KYC completion; CUPED not needed; stratified by channel; report absolute lift with 95% CI.

title: Assisted-KYC outreach for stalled applicants (backlog + new)
hypothesis: Applicants still pending beyond the historic maximum KYC lag (11 days; no KYC later than day 11 is observed) will not complete unaided; an assisted contact offer can recover some. Ticket raisers are a visible high-risk group (7.5% completion vs 74.9%).
target_segment: Mature registrants with KYC incomplete beyond day 11 (backlog of 2,687) plus new registrants as they cross day 11. Enrol only after reconciling KYC status with the activity log (about 91% of this group has a source conflict)
intervention: One outbound message offering assisted KYC (call-back or in-app chat link).
primary_metric: KYC completion within 30 days of the outreach date
guardrail_metrics: Support contacts per enrolled user; assisted-contact cost per completed KYC (operational cost only); complaint rate
baseline_source: ASSUMPTION: 2% unaided late recovery. The data show no KYC completions after day 11, so the true unaided rate is near 0 and cannot be estimated
expected_benefit: +6 pp recovery among stalled applicants is an ASSUMPTION. With a backlog of this size, even a small lift is detectable quickly, but the result applies to stalled users, not all registrants.
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test (exact test if counts are small) on 30-day completion; ITT analysis; stratify backlog vs new.

title: UPI-first bank link with alternate-method fallback
hypothesis: Bank-link failure/abandonment is a method-specific friction; offering UPI-based verification first and a one-tap fallback to net-banking reduces drop-off.
target_segment: KYC-completed users who have not linked a bank
intervention: Default to UPI-first linking; on failure, show alternate method and a status message within the same screen.
primary_metric: Bank linked within 7 days of KYC
guardrail_metrics: Bank-link failure rate; bank-link tickets per 100 KYC-complete users; fraud/mismatch flags
expected_benefit: +4 pp is ASSUMED. Bank-linking is the smallest bottleneck by users lost (784), so expected volume benefit is limited.
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test on 7-day bank-link rate; stratified by device (iOS/Android/Web).

title: Low-ticket first-deposit prompt with quick-amount chips
hypothesis: Users who have linked a bank but not deposited face an amount-decision barrier; showing low-ticket quick amounts anchored to the observed median first deposit (about Rs 6,400-6,500) lowers friction.
intervention: Quick-amount chips (e.g. 2,000 / 5,000 / 10,000) and a deposit reminder on day 3 and day 7.
primary_metric: First deposit within 14 days of bank link
guardrail_metrics: Withdrawal-to-deposit ratio in first 30 days (guard against low-intent deposits); deposit-related tickets; opt-out rate
expected_benefit: +5 pp is ASSUMED. First Deposit is the second-largest leak (1,305 users lost).
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test on 14-day deposit rate; secondary: median deposit amount (Mann-Whitney).

title: Guided first-trade walkthrough with a practice order
hypothesis: Funded-but-never-traded users lack confidence; an in-app walkthrough and a simulated/practice order will convert more deposits into first trades.
target_segment: Users with a deposit and no trade
intervention: Walkthrough card + practice (paper) order + day-2 and day-5 reminder.
primary_metric: First trade within 14 days of deposit
guardrail_metrics: Order-error/rejection rate; trading-support tickets; share of first trades that are very small (<Rs 500) to avoid hollow activation
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test on 14-day first-trade rate; check M1 activity as secondary to confirm that activation is not hollow.

title: Two-sided referral prompt at first-trade moment
hypothesis: Referral is the highest-quality, lowest-cost-per-trader channel (cost per first trader about Rs 438 vs Rs 1,050-1,250 elsewhere); surfacing the referral prompt right after a user's first trade will increase referred registrations.
target_segment: Active users (current MAU of 4,611) at launch, plus new first-time traders as they arrive
intervention: Share sheet + invite-link prompt after first trade; reward structure kept identical in both arms (only prompt placement varies).
control_group: Existing referral entry in menu only.
primary_metric: Referred registrations per 100 exposed users within 30 days
guardrail_metrics: Quality of referred users (first-trade rate of referred cohort must stay >= 45%); referral abuse/duplicate flags; opt-out rate
baseline_source: ACTUAL (approximate): mean monthly referral registrations / mean MAU. Referrer IDs are not in the dataset, so attribution is approximated
expected_benefit: +50% relative lift in the referral rate is ASSUMED (a small baseline requires a large relative effect to be detectable).
evaluation_method: Poisson/negative-binomial rate comparison per exposed user; guardrail on the first-trade rate of referred users.

title: Week-2 / month-1 habit nudges for first-time traders
hypothesis: Users who trade within months 0-1 retain better at month 3 (60.7% vs 50.0%, an association, not proven causal); a structured nudge after first trade can lift engagement.
target_segment: Users who have placed their first trade (launch pool = current first-time traders, then new first traders weekly)
intervention: Contextual, non-promotional nudges at day 7, 14, 21 after first trade (watch-list suggestions, goal reminders).
primary_metric: Active in calendar month 3 after registration (M3 retention)
guardrail_metrics: Notification opt-out rate; app-uninstall proxy; complaint tickets about notifications
baseline_source: ACTUAL: pooled M3 retention, all mature registrants (traders-only baseline is higher; not computed)
feasibility: Slow (14-26 weeks accrual): run concurrently with other tests or accept a larger MDE
expected_benefit: +6 pp M3 retention is ASSUMED. Note the early-warning logistic model was weak (CV AUC about 0.57), so targeting by predicted risk is NOT proposed.
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test on M3 active flag; pre-register stratification by channel; difference-in-differences not needed under randomisation.

title: In-flow KYC status tracker + contextual help
hypothesis: KYC & verification is the largest ticket category (22.7% of tickets, 17.3 tickets per 100 users) and 43% of KYC tickets are raised while KYC is still pending; a status tracker plus contextual help should deflect avoidable tickets.
intervention: KYC progress tracker with expected time, rejection reasons shown inline, and FAQ deflection before 'contact support'.
primary_metric: KYC tickets per registrant within 30 days
guardrail_metrics: KYC completion rate must not fall; CSAT for tickets; escalation rate; backlog age
baseline_source: ACTUAL: KYC & verification tickets / registered users (all-time per user)
feasibility: Slow (14-26 weeks accrual): run concurrently with other tests or accept a larger MDE
expected_benefit: -20% relative KYC ticket rate is ASSUMED.
evaluation_method: Rate comparison (Poisson/NB) on tickets per user; co-primary guardrail on KYC completion (non-inferiority).

title: Dormant-user win-back sequence (value-led, no incentive vs small incentive)
hypothesis: Users with no activity for 3+ months reactivate at a low base rate; a tailored win-back message can lift reactivation.
target_segment: Dormant users: no active month Aug-Oct 2026 (pool of 1,632 mature users), plus new entrants (about 113/week, ASSUMED to continue)
intervention: 3-touch win-back (email/push, 7 days apart) with product updates and a learning resource.
primary_metric: Reactivation: active in the 30 days after the last touch
guardrail_metrics: Unsubscribe rate; complaint rate; reactivated users' trading in the following month (to avoid empty logins)
baseline_source: ACTUAL: pooled P(active in month t | no activity in t-3..t-1) from Monthly_Activity
expected_benefit: +6 pp reactivation is ASSUMED. NOTE: the 34.7% base rate is high for a group labelled dormant; it reflects the synthetic activity pattern, so treat the baseline cautiously.
evaluation_method: Two-proportion z-test on 30-day reactivation; stratified by channel; ITT.

title: Pre-qualification landing page for Paid Social (CMP03 + CMP04)
hypothesis: Video Awareness (CMP04) has the weakest scorecard result (first-trade rate 30.8%, cost per first trader about Rs 1,250) and Education Social (CMP03) is also below average; intent-setting content before sign-up may filter low-intent registrants and raise first-trade yield per rupee.
target_segment: Paid Social click-throughs (CMP03 and CMP04 pooled so that traffic is sufficient)
intervention: Insert a short 'what you will need to start' page (KYC documents, bank, minimum amounts) before registration.
primary_metric: First trade within 45 days of registration
guardrail_metrics: Registrations per rupee (CAC must not rise by more than 20%); KYC completion; organic spill-over
baseline_source: ACTUAL: Paid Social mature first-trade rate (CMP03 + CMP04)
feasibility: Traffic-constrained (> 26 weeks): needs larger MDE, pooling, or a longer run
expected_benefit: +6 pp first-trade rate per registrant is ASSUMED; the volume trade-off must be evaluated per click.
evaluation_method: Compare first trades per 1,000 click-throughs (not per registrant) so that lower registration volume is not mistaken for higher quality. Click-through counts are not in the dataset and must be logged.
